seo.title: Truthound: Local CSV & Parquet Data Validation MCP
seo.description: Evaluate Truthound Local for CSV and Parquet data validation through MCP: missing values, duplicate rows, profiling, sampled PII checks and explicit limits.
seo.heading: Local CSV and Parquet data validation through MCP
seo.intro: Truthound is a data quality framework with a bounded Local MCP interface for AI assistants. Explore supported file checks, permission requirements and execution evidence before choosing a tool.

pages.title: Local CSV & Parquet Validation with MCP | Truthound
pages.description: Check which local CSV and Parquet validation tasks Truthound supports, how directory consent limits access, and what information can reach the host model.
pages.heading: Can an AI assistant check local CSV and Parquet files?
pages.intro: Use this guide when selecting an MCP tool for tabular quality checks before ingestion or analysis. Truthound Local covers missing values and duplicate rows; choosing it also requires understanding directory consent and which metadata leaves the local tool.

pages.title: Great Expectations Alternatives with MCP | Truthound Scope
pages.description: Considering a Great Expectations alternative with MCP? Compare Truthound Local’s bounded file checks with framework capabilities, configuration limits and evidence.
pages.heading: Evaluating a Great Expectations alternative with MCP support
pages.intro: Separate two decisions: choosing a data quality framework and choosing the operations an AI assistant can call. Truthound is a candidate when bounded local file checks meet the task. Its Local MCP surface is not a drop-in replacement for Great Expectations suites.

pages.title: Local Data Profiling & Sampled PII Screening | Truthound MCP
pages.description: Understand Truthound Local’s aggregate profiling and sampled PII screening for tabular datasets, including false negatives, metadata exposure and compliance limits.
pages.heading: What do local profiling and sampled PII checks establish?
pages.intro: Profiling and PII screening answer different preparation questions. Aggregate profiling describes observed data; sampled screening can flag likely sensitive content. Neither a clean sample nor observed column types establishes complete validation or compliance.
